fixer.title: perf: reduce renderer memory usage when reading large agentHost plugin files

cases.mechanism: The fallback base64 encoder appends four one-character strings for every three input bytes, creating O(n) concatenation operations and substantial transient string/rope allocation for large binary resource payloads.
cases.symptom: Large agent-host `resourceRead` responses encoded tens-of-megabyte files through this loop, producing severe transient memory growth and CPU time proportional to millions of JavaScript concatenations.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added `Uint8Array.prototype.toBase64` fast path performs the encoding natively and bypasses the per-character JavaScript concatenation loop when the runtime supports it.
cases.evidence: Agent-host filesystem resource providers call `encodeBase64(content.value)` for Base64 reads, and the old loop performs four `output +=` operations per three bytes. Added line 502 returns the native typed-array encoding before that loop. The PR's supplied 45 MiB profile reports the corresponding allocation and CPU spike collapsing after this path is used.
